summary_paragraph: A woman with ESRD on MWF hemodialysis via a left femoral tunneled catheter, HIV/AIDS on antiretroviral therapy and opportunistic infection prophylaxis, paroxysmal atrial fibrillation on warfarin, and recent MRSA catheter-related bacteremia on vancomycin with dialysis was admitted with dyspnea on exertion, lethargy, and generalized malaise after missing dialysis. On arrival she had hyperkalemia (K 6.5) and metabolic acidosis that improved with temporizing therapy (albuterol, insulin/dextrose, potassium binder) and subsequent hemodialysis; chest radiograph showed no acute intrathoracic abnormality and EKG had no ischemic or hyperkalemic changes. She experienced relative/asymptomatic hypotension that improved with a small IV fluid bolus and an increased midodrine regimen. Blood cultures showed no growth, and she continued vancomycin with hemodialysis to complete her prior MRSA treatment course. Symptoms improved after two dialysis sessions, and she was discharged home with services with plans to resume her regular dialysis schedule, continue warfarin with INR monitoring during dialysis, and follow up with primary care and specialty care for ongoing issues including eosinophilia/pruritus.
